text:
The Flames lost Kevin Bahl for the season, and that is the story hanging over everything else in Calgary right now. Bahl and Simon Nemec were the pair logging the most five-on-five minutes on the team, and the reporting since has been about the blue line options left and whether the Flames go shopping for a replacement.

The team he leaves behind is 9-10-1 with 19 points, and the process is thin: 47% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) and a power play producing only 0.38 expected goals a game. Our playoff odds sit at 14%. Saturday's 3-2 win in Los Angeles came from Yegor Sharangovich's late winner and a busy night for Dustin Wolf.

There are bright spots, and they're young. Zayne Parekh is becoming the power-play quarterback Calgary drafted him to be, and the headlines have noticed. Matvei Gridin scored in Los Angeles, playing on the line with Ryan Strome and Martin Pospisil that gets the most minutes. Devin Cooley has been the best story in net, .941 with 5.1 goals saved above expected over his last five starts.

What we'd watch: how the minutes Bahl leaves get split, and whether Parekh and the kids can lift a team whose chances say it's still a step behind.
